headline: Advances in Quantum Complexity and Hamiltonian Learning
summary: Today's research explores the limits of quantum simulation, Hamiltonian learning, and state preparation. The papers offer new algorithms for structured systems alongside rigorous lower bounds for non-Gaussian states and spin glasses.

themes.title: Hamiltonian Learning and Spectral Estimation
themes.body: New methods tackle the reconstruction of complex quantum systems. Researchers introduced SPICES for single-particle spectral estimation under global unitaries, while others developed polynomial-sample algorithms to learn dense Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev Hamiltonians.

themes.title: Complexity Bounds in Simulation and State Preparation
themes.body: Studies establish strict computational limits across diverse quantum models. This includes robust exponential lower bounds for Gaussian ranks in continuous variable systems, state preparation complexity limits in quantum spin glasses, and classical polynomial-time approaches for quantum impurity models.

themes.title: Permutation Symmetry and Communication
themes.body: Investigation into full permutation invariance reveals how symmetry constraints limit quantum communication advantages, demonstrating that asymptotic optimization can be reduced to a single channel use.

connections.body: Both papers utilize quantum de Finetti theorems or reductions as core analytical tools to tame complex many-body symmetries and derive bounds.
